content_html:
Website maintenance: what to update and how often

Website maintenance keeps your site secure, fast and up to date after launch. A maintenance checklist covers software and plugin updates, security patches, backups, uptime and malware monitoring, speed checks, broken-link fixes, content refreshes, SEO reviews and form testing. Apply security updates at least monthly, and review content and SEO every quarter.

Website maintenance checklist: what to update and how often

TaskHow often
Security patches, CMS and plugin updatesMonthly, or as soon as critical fixes appear
BackupsDaily or weekly, depending on how often content changes
Uptime and malware monitoringContinuous
Contact forms and checkout testsMonthly
Speed and Core Web Vitals checkMonthly
Broken links and 404 errorsMonthly
Content refresh and SEO reviewQuarterly
Restore test from backupQuarterly

Why website maintenance matters

  • Security. Most hacks use known holes that an update would have closed.
  • Speed. Sites slow down over time as content and plugins pile up.
  • Rankings. Fresh, working pages keep search engines and visitors happy.
  • Leads. A broken form can quietly cost you enquiries for weeks.

Website backup and recovery best practices

  1. Back up automatically, as often as your content changes.
  2. Keep copies off the server, in a separate location.
  3. Keep several versions, not just the latest one.
  4. Test a restore regularly, and write down the steps.

Website hosting vs website maintenance

Hosting is the server, storage and network your site runs on. Maintenance, on the other hand, is the ongoing care: updates, security, backups, speed tuning and support. So you need both, and they often come from different providers. Therefore, be clear about who is responsible for what.

What can you do yourself?

Many businesses update their own text, images and blog posts through the CMS. However, leave software updates, security, backups and speed work to someone who can test changes safely and fix problems quickly.

How much does website maintenance cost?

In India, maintenance usually costs ₹1,500 to ₹25,000 a month, depending on the size of the site and the services included. For example, a common rule of thumb is to budget 15 to 20 percent of the original build cost each year. See more in our website cost guide.

When maintenance is no longer enough

Finally, if your site is slow, hard to update, looks dated or no longer converts, it may be time for a redesign rather than more patches. Read the signs in our website redesign guide.

A simple website maintenance plan

First, set a monthly website maintenance routine: update the CMS, plugins and themes, check backups and scan for malware. Next, review speed every quarter. For example, test your key pages on Core Web Vitals and fix the slowest ones. In addition, check forms, links and checkout so nothing breaks quietly. Then refresh content. Old prices, dates and team details hurt trust and SEO. Also review analytics to see which pages bring leads and which lose visitors. As a result, small fixes stay small, and you avoid paying for a full rebuild later. However, if the site is slow, hard to update or no longer fits your brand, maintenance alone may not be enough. In that case, plan a redesign. Finally, keep a simple log of every change, so problems are easy to trace.
